newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish yields end down in foreign driven trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish yields end down in foreign driven trade.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swedish debt yields ended the day lower on Monday, helped by stronger foreign markets.
A comment by Finance Minister Erik Asbrink that he saw no problems with a European Union recommendation on how the country should reduce its budget deficit may have lent support, dealers said.
* Six-month T-bill rates flat at 4.20 percent
* Ten-year bond yields lost three basis points to 7.00 percent
* Crown firms to 4.5200 against the mark vs 4.5330 late Friday
Swedish long debt yields opened higher but ended lower on Monday, mirroring moves on foreign markets.
"We are somewhat at a crossroads now. The technical level for the ten-year bond yields is at 7.00 percent and for the two-year bond yields, somewhere between 4.75 and 4.80 percent," one dealer said.

A statement by Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink that he saw no problems with a European Union recommendation on how the country should reduce its budget deficit may have lent support, dealers said.
Six-month T-bill rates closed flat at 4.20 percent and ten-year bond yields fell three basis points to 7.00 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.5200 from 4.5330 late on Friday.
